transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-03
Time: 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Liam (Constellation PM), Sofia (Constellation SE), Ava (Constellation Marketplace Ops)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for the joint solution (Redwood Dedicated + Constellation Aurora offering), and next steps for a co-sell listing. Discussed integration touchpoints (billing, SSO, deployment templates), performance benchmark plan, and security/compliance checklist for marketplace onboarding.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing flow and required artifacts
- Reference architecture (VPC peering, private deployments, KMS integration)
- Joint solution deployment templates (Helm/CloudFormation/Terraform)
- Benchmarks and validation plan
- Legal/compliance contacts and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, um thanks for joining, i think we've got about 45 minutes, so we'll try to keep it tight. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Jon our SE will talk through the infra things and benchmarks.
[00:22] Liam: hey maya, thanks, excited to sync. quick note, ava's going to be focused on marketplace ops requirements so she'll jump in when we get to that section.
[00:35] Ava: yep thanks liam, hi all.
[00:40] Jon: cool, i'll share my screen in a sec with the high level ref arch, but first can we confirm what listing type you're aiming for — marketplace listing only, or joint solution with co-sell & managed offering?
[00:55] Sofia: for Constellation, goal is marketplace listing with a reference arch and joint-solution docs. we'd like a co-branded listing and the ability to spin up a managed deployment via our Aurora marketplace flow.
[01:10] Maya: perfect, that's what we expected. so the three buckets we need to close: listing assets (copy, logos, screenshots), deployment templates + IaC, and billing/integration touchpoints (metering/pricing).
[01:25] Liam: and security — SOC2/ISO and kms integration are must-haves for our enterprise customers, also SSO via saml.
[01:35] Jon: yep, we've done KMS + HSM integrations before. one thing to flag, in our private deploy we support customer-managed KMS keys and audit logs; for the marketplace managed flow we can either bring-your-own-key or use our managed key depending on the customer profile.
[01:55] Ava: policy-wise marketplace requires we document the KMS flow and provide an SOC2 attestation link. can you share the attestation doc?
[02:10] Maya: yes, i'll share our SOC2 report and the security FAQ.
[02:18] Jon: moving onto the ref arch — i'm going to call out a couple of variants: 1) Marketplace-managed deployment (Redwood Dedicated running in Constellation's Aurora region via marketplace provisioning), 2) Customer-provisioned private deployment (VPC + private control plane), and 3) Hybrid where control plane is managed + data plane in customer VPC.
[02:40] Jon: i'll drop a quick ascii diagram: 
- Marketplace-managed: provisioning lambda -> infra templating -> dedicated pool -> tde(?) KV cache -> autoscaling
(notation is rough, apologies for ascii)
[03:05] Sofia: quick q — for the dedicated pools, do you support node pinning by tenant? we have enterprise customers who want dedicated infra.
[03:15] Jon: yes, dedicated pools with tenant isolation are supported, we call out GPU pool reservation and hard partitioning. there are a few tradeoffs — unit cost goes up but you get predictable latency.
[03:28] Liam: perfect. for marketplace we need to capture the SLA and latency targets in the listing. do you have standard numbers?
[03:38] Maya: we publish performance profiles per model; for the ref arch we can include typical p95 latencies for the curated models on Aurora gpus, but we'll mark them as 'typical' versus guaranteed — guarantees are part of Dedicated contracts.
[03:55] Ava: on the listing assets, we need a short 50-100 word description, a longer 400-600 word product overview, 3 screenshots, and a video ideally. Also legal contact and logos in svg.
[04:12] Maya: noted. i'll put together the copy and visuals.
[04:18] Jon: about IaC, we provide Helm charts and Terraform modules for private + dedicated. marketplace provisioning will likely want CloudFormation templates or a Terraform module that plugs into Constellation's provisioning flow.
[04:34] Sofia: Constellation prefers Terraform modules for Aurora marketplace. can you version the module and include example variables for region, instance types, and kv cache sizes?
[04:46] Jon: yes, we'll add variables for region, instance_type (gpu family), sequence_length defaults, and kv_cache_size. we'll also include a default policy for autoscaling and burst.
[04:59] Liam: excellent. another integration question: logging and tracing — is there a standard for sending logs to our observability stack?
[05:07] Jon: Redwood Console supports exporting traces and logs via webhooks and also has sinks for common providers. For Constellation's managed offering we can push traces to your observability endpoint via secure forwarder. note: sampling config may differ.
[05:24] Ava: okay, we'll need a security appendix that details network ports, IP ranges, and cert rotation policies — marketplace ops requires that to approve the listing.
[05:35] Maya: we'll compile a security appendix and include the network diagram.
[05:40] 
[10:12] Jon: jumping ahead to performance validation — we propose two benchmark vectors: 1) latency-focused: small batch, short sequences 128 tokens, measure p50/p95; 2) throughput-focused: batching with sequences 512-1024, measure tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens.
[10:30] Sofia: that makes sense. can you run those on our Aurora test cluster (dev account)? we can provision a sandbox if you send a runbook.
[10:40] Jon: yes we can. i'll need access creds to the sandbox and a terraform sample to spin up the infra. do you have any limitations around quota?
[10:50] Liam: we'll provision a small quota for test runs, specify the instance families you want. also note that for end-to-end we need to test on the same model you're listing in the marketplace listing — e.g., the redwood-curie or a curated open model.
[11:05] Jon: we'll align on the model. reminder — model variants and quantization impact perf; we'll include both fp16 and int8 runs so you can compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
[11:20] 
[17:02] Maya: quick question on billing — Constellation marketplace expects two flows: marketplace billing (customer billed via Constellation, Constellation remits to Redwood) or direct billing where customer signs with Redwood. which ones do you support?
[17:18] Ava: marketplace ops prefers marketplace-billing for managed offerings, but we need to capture pricing granularity — per-token with tiered discounts, or per-instance reserved pricing for Dedicated.
[17:33] Maya: we support per-token usage and reserved capacity. for marketplace-billing we'll need to wire pricing API (metering hooks) and agree on settlement cadence.
[17:45] Liam: what's the typical integration effort for metering hooks?
[17:50] Jon: technically it's an HTTP webhook where we emit usage records; we can batch them. we'll provide an open API spec for metering ingestion. typical dev effort for end-to-end wiring is ~2-3 sprint tasks plus security review.
[18:05] Ava: ok note that marketplace security runs a pen test before approving managed listings — you'll need to coordinate.
[18:12] Maya: understood. we'll scope that in the timeline.
[18:18] 
[25:00] Sofia: regarding reference arch docs, can you provide an example deployment walkthrough for a customer-provisioned private deployment? we want step-by-step for our docs team.
[25:12] Jon: absolutely, we'll produce a reference repo with: terraform/helm, sample k8s manifests, network diagram, KMS integration steps, and a troubleshooting section. we'll include a sample load test script.
[25:28] Liam: also include a roll-back playbook and canary/blue-green rollout examples. those are big asks from eng teams.
[25:38] Jon: yes canary and A/B rollouts are supported; we'll include config snippets for rollouts. note: for model rollouts we support automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency breaches SLOs.
[25:52] Sofia: great.
[26:00] 
[33:10] Ava: timeline check — marketplace ops needs final listing assets two weeks prior to marketplace release window. what's your ideal timeline?
[33:22] Maya: if we aim for a release window around 2026-03-15, we need final assets by 2026-03-01. that aligns with your two-week buffer.
[33:34] Liam: works for us, but we also need the benchmark data earlier, say by 2026-02-14, so we can validate claimed performance.
[33:44] Jon: that's doable. bench runs by 2/10 and data posted by 2/14 to give you time.
[33:52] Ava: legal/partner agreements — we'll need a named legal contact, standard MSA addendum for marketplace.
[33:59] Maya: i'll loop in our legal, but for now point person is Maya (AE) and billing is handled by our partnerships finance team — i'll include contacts in the doc.
[34:10] 
[40:00] Jon: ok final recap from SE side: we'll produce ref-arch repo, terraform/helm modules, benchmark results (fp16 and int8), and metering API spec.
[40:12] Maya: i'll draft marketplace copy, collect logos, share SOC2 and security appendix.
[40:20] Ava: we'll provide marketplace requirements checklist and a staging sandbox provision.
[40:27] Liam: and i'll coordinate internal product for the go/no-go on the release window.
[40:33] 
[43:00] Maya: great, next steps — i'll send the draft listing + security docs by friday 2026-02-06. Jon will run bench and post results by 2026-02-10. Ava to provide marketplace artifacts by 2026-02-05. we'll meet again week of 2026-02-16 for the reference arch review.
[43:20] Sofia: thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
[43:27] Jon: thanks all.
[43:30] Maya: thanks, bye.
